chapter: Blackbirds, Carmen Jones and the Ziegfeld Follies
title: The song This Is My Last Affair
summary: He recalls and sings part of a song he liked from the Follies, written by a man in the show.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: What we played: tunes and repertoire in the early days

blocks.x: Can you tell me any of the other jokes or songs -- did you sing any other song? Can you sing me one of the songs that you did at the Ziegfeld Follies?

That's not easy to think of either -- song I sign in the Follies. One of the songs I did at the Follies -- what was it -- I'll have to think about that. The name of the song I like to sing, I liked it so well, I liked to sing it, 'It Sure was a Last Affair.' "Can't you see, what love and romance has done to me I'm not the same as I used to be This is my last affair. Melody, keeps on rounded like a melody (Inaudible) that is just for me This is my last affair. Right from the start you took my heart Broke it right in two Can't you see what you've done to me (Inaudible) misery. Gone again. (Hums) This is my last affair. I can't think of the words no more than that.
That's a pretty song, though, you know. Do you know who it's by?

Yes, by one of the fellas in the show -- what was his name? I forgot his name. I've got his music somewhere, I don't know where. "Last Affair." Can't think of the words to that song. But that's the way it leaves you, and when it leaves you it leaves, especially when you get older. But anyway, if I get the words, I'll put it on a cassette for you. If I can get the words to it. I've got to finish that other song I was going to put on the thing for you, too.
